question: Before formal hospitals existed, what was the main basis of healthcare in ancient civilizations?
explanation: You've got this! Before modern science, early societies relied on community care, traditional herbs, and spiritual explanations to make sense of illnesses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: How did the ancient Greek philosopher Hippocrates help change how people viewed disease?

options.A: He proved that all illnesses were caused by evil spirits
options.B: He introduced modern surgical antibiotics to the Mediterranean
options.C: He banned the use of traditional herbal remedies entirely
options.D: He taught that disease came from natural bodily imbalances

explanation: Great job! Hippocrates moved medical thinking away from pure superstition by connecting illness to natural causes inside the body. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: During the Middle Ages, which group set up the earliest institutionalized hospitals?
explanation: Spot on! Christian religious orders played a huge role back then, sheltering and caring for the sick as an act of charity. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: What major historical event during the Middle Ages led directly to the creation of military nursing orders?

options.C: The discovery of the New World
options.D: The Fall of the Roman Empire

explanation: Exactly! The Crusades created an urgent need for organized battlefield transport and care, giving rise to groups like the Knights Hospitaller. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: Where did Florence Nightingale famously lower soldier death rates during wartime?

options.A: A monastery hospital in medieval Rome
options.B: A military camp in colonial Nigeria
options.D: Scutari hospital during the Crimean War

explanation: Well done! Nightingale introduced strict cleanliness and ventilation at Scutari, saving countless lives during the Crimean War. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why was opening the Nightingale Training School in 1860 such a big deal for nursing?

options.A: It replaced doctors with fully independent nurse practitioners
options.B: It funded free hospitals across the British Empire
options.C: It transformed nursing into a disciplined, respected profession
options.D: It made military service compulsory for all female nurses

explanation: You got it! By founding a formal school, she turned nursing into a legitimate career that required proper training rather than just basic housework. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Who set up the earliest formal Western-style nurse training programs right here in Nigeria?
explanation: Spot on! Christian missions introduced Western-style hospitals and began training local Nigerians in professional nursing care during the colonial era. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: How did Nigerian healthcare and nursing shift right after independence in 1960?

options.A: All hospitals were handed back exclusively to foreign missionary groups
options.B: Western medicine was completely banned in favor of traditional herbs
options.C: Nursing education was moved entirely out of the country
options.D: The government assumed control and expanded national training standards

explanation: Exactly! Gaining independence meant local control, the setup of national regulatory councils, and the growth of professional nursing education structures. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: What was a common feature of early hospital-based nursing apprenticeships?

options.A: Exclusive focus on advanced medical pharmacology
options.B: Heavy reliance on student labor to run hospital wards
options.C: Guaranteed university degrees upon completion of training
options.D: Complete freedom from hospital service duties

explanation: You got this! Early training schools often used student nurses as the main workforce to keep the wards running, sometimes putting hospital chores ahead of classroom learning. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary job of nursing regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council?

options.A: To set practice standards and protect the public
options.B: To hire and fire doctors in public health clinics
options.C: To manage hospital budgets and purchase medical equipment
options.D: To run political campaigns for healthcare workers

explanation: Spot on! Regulatory councils handle licensing, school accreditations, and ethics to make sure patients always receive safe and quality care. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a current challenge facing nursing today, both globally and in Nigeria?

options.A: Managing rising rates of chronic illnesses
options.C: Migration of skilled nurses to other countries
options.D: An excess of unassigned hospital nursing jobs

explanation: Well done! There certainly isn't an excess of jobs—instead, our health systems face severe shortages, heavy workloads, and the migration of skilled professionals. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)

question: How has modern technology changed everyday nursing practice in today's healthcare world?

options.A: Technology has completely removed the need for direct physical patient assessment
options.B: Digital tools and electronic records have transformed documentation and care delivery
options.C: Computers have replaced doctors and nurses in rural community clinics
options.D: Digital systems have slowed down medication administration everywhere

explanation: You nailed it! Electronic health records and digital tools make it much easier for nurses to track patient progress and communicate across distances. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)
